short: Luminescent Erbium-Doped Silicon Thin Films for Advanced Ant
title: Luminescent Erbium-Doped Silicon Thin Films for Advanced Anti-Counterfeit Labels

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Anti-counterfeit labels need data that stays unreadable in an optical or scanning electron microscope. Selective fs-laser irradiation of an Er/Si bilayer should dope Er into silicon locally, giving 1530 nm luminescent pixels.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/deposition), n6 (PRC/treatment), n7 (PRC/treatment), n8 (PRC/treatment), n16 (DES/down_select)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Irradiated zones contain crystalline silicon grains. Erbium is incorporated into the silicon matrix of the irradiated spots as optically active Er:O complexes.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (STR/phase/identity), n10 (STR/chemistry/composition), n12 (STR/microstructure/feature_size). Premises: The 520 cm-1 Raman line is the TO mode of crystalline silicon; nanometre grains shift it downward

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Local laser heating crystallises the amorphous silicon and drives erbium in-diffusion from the overlayer into it. Oxidation during irradiation in air surrounds Er3+ with oxygen, and Er:O in silica emits more strongly than Er in silicon.
states.detail: Absorbed: m1 (MEC/pathway), m2 (MEC/pathway), n13 (PRP/value), n14 (PRP/value). Premises: Erbium ions surrounded by oxygen atoms glow more brightly than erbium surrounded by silicon

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The label reads as a QR code in the 1530 nm PL map but as a featureless hole array in reflected light

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Laser-written erbium-doped silicon spots give a two-level anti-counterfeit label readable only by 1530 nm photoluminescence mapping

nodes.title: RAMAN, F2, F3
nodes.head: A sharp peak near 520 cm-1 appears in the Raman spectra after laser exposure and is absent in the initial film. Raman intensity at 518 cm-1 rises to a maximum near 3 mJ/cm2, then collapses above 4 mJ/cm2.
nodes.solves: Irradiated zones contain crystalline silicon grains
nodes.op: compare across conditions, cross check consistency, read trend
nodes.note: the initial and 0.5 mJ/cm2 traces are marked x5 and all five traces are vertically offset, so peak heights are not directly comparable across traces blue triangles, left axis: about 50 a.u. at 1 mJ/cm2, 310 a.u. at 2.8-3 mJ/cm2, 85 a.u. at 4-6 and about 20 a.u. above 8 panel citation dropped: crop F3b carries cue class 'micrograph', which the cue map does not allow for RAMAN. The 4.2 mJ/cm2 spot is barely above background, the 5.7 spot is the brightest F2c has the 518 cm-1 signal near zero above 8 mJ/cm2, while the F3 linked text puts the crystallisation threshold at 4.8 mJ/cm2 and F3a/F3b show modification and crystalline signal growing from 4.2 to 6.4 mJ/cm2: the two figures use incompatible fluence scales
nodes.detail: o1: A sharp peak near 520 cm-1 appears in the Raman spectra after laser exposure and is absent in the initial film; o2: Raman intensity at 518 cm-1 rises to a maximum near 3 mJ/cm2, then collapses above 4 mJ/cm2; o8: The 518 cm-1 Raman map places the crystalline signal on the three higher-fluence spots only; o16: Figure 2c puts the crystalline maximum near 3 mJ/cm2, where Figure 3 still shows it growing at 6.4
